49:1: God the Most High means by His statement: O you who have believed: O you who have acknowledged the Oneness of God and the Prophethood of Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Do not precede God and His Messenger means: Do not rush to decide a matter in your wars or your religion before God and His Messenger decide it for you, lest you decide contrary to the command of God and the command of His Messenger. It is narrated from the Arabs that someone precedes his leader, meaning he hastens to command or prohibit before him. The people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about this, although their wording differed in explaining its meaning. Who said that? Ali told us: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Do not put yourself before God and His Messenger, meaning: Do not say anything contrary to the Book and the Sunnah. Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement, O you who have believed, do not put yourselves forward before God and His Messenger… the verse. He said: They were forbidden to speak before His speech. Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, O you who have believed, do not put yourselves forward before God and His Messenger, he said: Do not make an attempt to attack the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with anything until God decrees it through his tongue. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada: O you who have believed, do not put yourselves forward before God and His Messenger. It was mentioned to us that some people used to say: If such and such had been revealed, such and such would have been removed. So God, the Almighty and Majestic, disliked that and put it forward. Al-Hasan said: Some Muslims slaughtered before the prayer of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the Day of Sacrifice, so the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered them to slaughter again. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement, O you who have believed, do not put yourselves forward before God and His Messenger, he said: Some people used to say, If only it had been revealed about such and such, if only it had been revealed about such and such. Al-Hasan said: They were people who slaughtered before the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered them to slaughter again. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, O you who have believed, do not put yourselves forward before God and His Messenger, meaning by that in fighting, and among their affairs was that which could not be decided except by His command, which was among the laws of their religion. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said regarding the words of God Almighty: O you who have believed, do not put yourselves forward before God and His Messenger, he said: Do not decide the matter before God and His Messenger. Ibn Humayd narrated: Mihran narrated to us on the authority of Sufyan, O you who have believed, do not precede God and His Messenger. He said: Do not decide a matter without the Messenger of God. The reciters of the regions read it with a damma on the ta’ in the phrase do not precede. This is the reading which I do not permit any contradiction to, due to the consensus of the authoritative reciters on it. It has been reported from the Arabs that they said: I preceded in such-and-such and I advanced in such-and-such. Based on this language, if it had been said: Do not precede with a fatha on the ta’, it would have been permissible. And His statement, “And fear God. Indeed, God is Hearing and Knowing.” He says: And fear God, O you who believe, in your speech, lest you say what God or His Messenger has not given you permission to say, and in other matters of yours, and be mindful of Him, for God is Hearing of what you say, Knowing of what you intend by your speech when you say it. Nothing of what is in your hearts is hidden from Him, and other matters of yours and the matters of others.
49:2: God Almighty says: O you who have believed in God and His Messenger, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Messenger of God, speaking harshly to him or speaking harshly to him. And do not speak loudly to him as you speak loudly to one another. He says: And do not call him as you call one another: O Muhammad, O Prophet of God, O Prophet of God, O Messenger of God. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And do not speak loudly to him as you speak loudly to one another, he said: Do not call out to him loudly, but speak softly, O Messenger of God. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And do not speak loudly to him as you speak loudly to one another, they used to speak loudly and raise their voices, so God admonished them and forbade them from doing that. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Qatada that they used to raise their voices and speak loudly in the presence of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so they were admonished and forbidden from doing so. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us: I heard Ad-Dahhak say about His statement, Do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet… the verse, it is like His statement, Do not make the calling of the Messenger among you like the calling of one of you to another (al-Nur 24:63). God forbade them from calling him as they call one another and commanded them to honor him and respect him, and to call him, if they called him, by the name of prophethood. Abu Kurayb narrated: Zaid Abu Thabit bin Thabit Qais bin Ash-Shammas narrated: My paternal uncle Ismail bin Muhammad bin Thabit bin Qais bin Shammas narrated on the authority of his father, who said: “When this verse was revealed: ‘Do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet or speak loudly to him,’ Thabit sat in the road weeping. Then Asim bin Adi of Banu Al-Ajlan passed by him and said: ‘What makes you weep, Thabit?’ He said: ‘Because of this verse. I fear that it was revealed about me, as I have a loud voice.’ So Asim bin Adi went to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and weeping overcame him. Then he went to his wife Jamila bint Abdullah bin Abi bin Salul and said to her: ‘When you enter my horse’s house, tie a nail to the reins.’ So she struck him with a nail until he came out and he turned away and said: ‘I will not come out until God takes me or the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) is pleased with me.’ Asim came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and told him what had happened. He said: ‘Go and call him for me.’ Then Asim went to the place, but did not find him. So he went to his family and found him in the horse’s house. He said to him: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) is calling you. He said: Break the lizard. So they went out and came to the Prophet of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to him: What makes you cry, Thabit? He said: I have a loud voice, and I fear that this verse was revealed about: “Do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet or speak loudly to him.” The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to him: Are you not satisfied to live a praiseworthy life, be killed as a martyr, and enter Paradise? He said: I am satisfied with the glad tidings of God and His Messenger. I will never raise my voice against the Messenger of God. Then God revealed: Indeed, those who lower their voices in the presence of the Messenger of God - those are the ones whose hearts God has tested for piety... the verse. Ibn Humayd narrated: Yaqub narrated to us, on the authority of Hafs, on the authority of Shimr ibn Atiyyah, who said: Thabit ibn Qays ibn Ash-Shammas came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he was sad. He said: O Thabit, what do I see with you? He said: I recited a verse last night, and I fear that it has rendered my deeds worthless: O you who have believed, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet. He had deafness in his ears, so say: O Prophet of God, I fear that I have raised my voice and spoken loudly to you, and that my deeds have been rendered worthless, and I am unaware. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Walk on the earth vigorously, for you are among the people of Paradise. Yaqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Aliyah narrated to us, saying: Ayyub narrated to us, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said: “When the verse: ‘O you who have believed, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet…’ was revealed, Thabit ibn Qays said: ‘I used to raise my voice above the voice of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and speak loudly, but I am from the people of Hellfire.’ So he stayed in his house, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, checked on him and asked about him. A man said: ‘He is my neighbor, and if you wish, I can tell you about him.’ He said: ‘Yes.’ So he came to him and said: ‘The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, checked on you and asked about you.’ He said: ‘This verse was revealed: ‘O you who have believed, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet…’ and I used to raise my voice above the voice of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and speak loudly to him, but I am from the people of Hellfire.’ So he went back to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and informed him. Thabit said: ‘Rather, he is from the people of Paradise.’ When the Day of Yamamah came, the people fled. So he said: ‘Fie on these people and what they worship!’ Fie upon these people and what they are doing! O group of Ansar, leave me something so that I may pray in its sea for an hour. He said: And a man was standing on a breach, and he was killed and he was killed.” Ibn Abd al-A'la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Zuhri, that Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas said: When the verse, Do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet, was revealed, he said: "O Prophet of God, I feared that I might be ruined. God has forbidden us to raise our voices above your voice, and I am a man with a loud voice. God has forbidden a person to like to be praised for what he has not done, but I find myself loving to be praised. God has forbidden arrogance, and I find myself loving wealth." The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: O Thabit, are you not satisfied to live a life of praise, be killed as a martyr, and enter Paradise? So he lived a life of praise and was killed as a martyr on the day of Musaylimah." Ali ibn Sahl told me: Muammil told us: Nafi’ ibn Umar ibn Jamil al-Jumahi told us: Ibn Abi Mulaykah told me, on the authority of al-Zubayr, who said: “A delegation - I think he said Tamim - came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, among them was al-Aqra’ ibn Habis. Abu Bakr asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to appoint him over his people. Umar said: Do not do that, O Messenger of God. They spoke until their voices were raised in the presence of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Abu Bakr said to Umar: You only wanted to contradict me. Umar said: I did not want to contradict you. Then the Qur’an was revealed: ‘O you who have believed, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet…’ until His saying: ‘and a great reward.’ Umar did not tell the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, after that, so that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, could hear him. Ibn al-Zubayr did not mention his grandfather, meaning Abu Bakr.” His statement, That your deeds may not be rendered worthless, means that your deeds may not be rendered worthless and become in vain, with no reward for you, nor any recompense for you raising your voices above the voice of your Prophet, and speaking loudly to him as you speak loudly to one another. The Arab scholars differed about the meaning of this. Some grammarians of Kufa said: It means: May your deeds not be in vain. Qatal: It has the jussive and nominative cases when it is placed in place of an. He said: In the reading of Abdullah, it is fatahatab a’malakum, which is evidence for the permissibility of the jussive case. Some grammarians of Basra said: He said: lest your deeds be in vain: meaning, for fear that your deeds be in vain. It may also be said: He leaned the wall lest it lean. And his saying, And you do not perceive, means: And you do not know and you do not realize.
49:3: God Almighty says: Those who refrain from raising their voices before the Messenger of God. The root of ghad is to refrain from speaking softly. And from it: lowering the gaze, which is refraining from looking, as Jarir said: Turn a blind eye, you are from Namir. You have not reached Kaab nor Kalb. And His statement, Those are the ones whose hearts God has tested for piety, God Almighty says: These are the ones who lower their voices in the presence of the Messenger of God, and they are the ones whose hearts God has tested by testing them, so He chose them and purified them for piety, meaning for fearing Him by performing His acts of obedience and avoiding His disobedience, just as gold is tested by fire, so its good is purified and its bad is removed. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said: Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, God tested their hearts, he said: Be sincere. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, God tested their hearts, he said: God purified their hearts in what He loved. His saying, For them is forgiveness, means that they will have from God pardon for their past sins, and a pardon from Him for them. And a great reward, means that they will have a generous reward, which is Paradise.
49:4: God Almighty says to his prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Indeed, those who call to you from behind your chambers… Chamber is the plural of chamber, and three is a stone, then it is pluralized and said: chambers and rooms. Some Arabs pluralize stone as rooms with a fatha on the jim, and likewise every plural of three to ten on fa’al they pluralize it as fa’al with a fatha on the second, and the nominative is more eloquent and better, and from this the poet said: Wasn't Ibad worthy of the drama of Balli and the verses of Al-Hujurat? He says: Yes, and for the Banu Hashim. His saying, And most of them do not reason, means: Most of them are ignorant of the religion of God, and what is necessary for them is your right and your respect. He mentioned that this verse and the one after it were revealed about a group of Bedouins who came calling to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from behind his rooms: O Muhammad, come out to us. The narrator mentioned that: Abu Ammar al-Marzouqi and al-Hasan ibn al-Harith told us: Al-Fadl ibn Musa told us, on the authority of al-Husayn ibn Waqid, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of al-Baraa’, regarding His statement, Indeed, those who call to you from behind the chambers, he said: “A man came to the Prophet, peace and blessings of God be upon him, and said: O Muhammad, my praise is adornment, and my blame is disgrace. He said: That is God, blessed and exalted.” Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wadh told us: Al-Hussein told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Baraa, with a similar narration, except that he said: That is God Almighty. Al-Hasan bin Arfa narrated to us: Al-Mu'tamir bin Sulayman Al-Taymi narrated to us: I heard Dawud Al-Tafawi say: I heard Abu Muslim Al-Bajali narrating on the authority of Zayd bin Arqam who said: “Some Arabs came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and some of them said to each other: Let us go to this man. If he is a prophet, we will be the luckiest people because of him, and if he is a king, we will live in his wing. So I went to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and informed him of that. Then they came to the room of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and began to call out to him: O Muhammad! So God revealed to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: ‘Indeed, those who call to you from behind the chambers, most of them do not reason.’ He said: Then the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took hold of my ear and stretched it out, and began to say: God has fulfilled your word, O Zayd. God has fulfilled your word, O Zayd.” Al-Hasan bin Abi Yahya Al-Muqaddami told us: Affan told us: Wahib told us: Musa bin Uqbah told us on the authority of Abu Salamah: Al-Aqra’ bin Habis Al-Tamimi told us that he came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and called out to him, saying: O Muhammad, my praising you is adornment, but my cursing you is disgraceful. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came out to him and said: Woe to you, that is God. Then God revealed: Indeed, those who call to you from behind the chambers… Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Indeed, those who call to you from behind the chambers: the Bedouins of Banu Tamim. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada: “A man came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and called out to him from behind a stone, saying: ‘O Muhammad, my praise is an adornment, and my cursing is a disgrace.’ So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came out to him and said: ‘Woe to you, that is God.’ Then God revealed: ‘Indeed, those who call to you from behind the chambers, most of them do not reason.’” Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada: “His statement, ‘Indeed, those who call to you from behind the chambers…’… the verse. It was mentioned to us that a man began to call out, ‘O Prophet of God, O Muhammad.’ So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came out to him and said, ‘What is the matter with you?’ He said, ‘By God, his praise is adornment, and his censure is disgrace.’ So the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, ‘That is God.’ So the man turned away, and it was mentioned to us that the man was a poet.” Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Habib bin Abi Umrah, who said: Bishr bin Ghalib and Labid bin Uttar, or Bishr bin Uttar and Labid bin Ghalib, were sitting with Al-Hajjaj. Bishr bin Ghalib said to Labid bin Uttar: Indeed, those who call to you from behind the chambers was revealed about your people, Banu Tamim. I mentioned that to Saeed bin Jubair, and he said: If he had known the end of the verse, he would have answered him: They do you a favor by becoming Muslims. They said: We have become Muslims, and Banu Asad did not fight you. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Al-Mubarak bin Fadala, on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said: “A Bedouin came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, from behind his rooms and said: ‘O Muhammad, O Muhammad.’ The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came out to him and said: ‘What is the matter with you? What is the matter with you?’ He said: ‘You know that my praising you is adornment and that my blaming you is ugliness.’ The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘That is God’s will.’ Then the verse was revealed: ‘O you who have believed, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet.’” The reciters differed in their recitation of his statement, from behind the rooms. The regions recited it with a damma on the ha’ and the jim from al-hujurat, except for Abu Ja’far al-Qari’, who recited it with a damma on the ha’ and a fatha on the jim, as I described, the plural of al-hujr is hujr, then the plural of al-hujr is hujrat. The correct reading for us is to pronounce both letters with a damma, as described before.
49:5: And His statement, And if they had been patient until you came out to them, it would have been better for them, God Almighty says: And if these people who call to you, O Muhammad, from behind the chambers, had been patient and did not call to you until you came out to them when you came out, it would have been better for them in the sight of God, because God has commanded them to respect and honor you, so by not calling to you they are leaving what God has forbidden them from. And God is Forgiving and Merciful, God Almighty says: God is Forgiving of the one who calls to you from behind the veil, if he repents from disobeying God by calling to you likewise, and returns to God’s command in that and other matters, and He is Merciful to him that He does not punish him for his sin after he has repented from it.
49:6: God Almighty says: O you who have believed in God and His Messenger, If a wicked person comes to you with information about a people, then verify it. The reciters differed in their reading of the statement fatabayyinu. The majority of the reciters of Medina read it fatabattu with a tha’, and it was mentioned that in Abdullah’s copy of the Qur’an it is dotted with a tha’. Some of the reciters read it fatabayyinu with a ba’, meaning: wait until you know its authenticity, do not rush to accept it. This is also the meaning of fatabattu. The correct thing to say about this is that they are two well-known readings with similar meanings, so whichever one the reader reads, he is correct. It was mentioned that this verse was revealed about Al-Walid bin Uqba bin Abi Mu’ayt. Mention the reason why this was said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us: Ja`far ibn `Awn narrated to us, on the authority of Musa ibn `Ubaydah, on the authority of Thabit, the freed slave of Umm Salamah, on the authority of Umm Salamah, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent a man to collect the alms of Banu al-Mustaliq after the battle. The people heard about that and met him, venerating the matter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Satan told him that they wanted to kill him. He returned to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: Banu al-Mustaliq have withheld their alms. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Muslims became angry. The people heard of his return. They came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and lined up before him when he had prayed the noon prayer. They said: ‘We seek refuge in God from the wrath of God and the wrath of His Messenger. You have sent us a man to collect alms.’ We were pleased with that and our eyes were comforted by it. Then he returned from some of the way, and we feared that this was wrath from God and His Messenger. They continued speaking to him until Bilal came and called the call to the afternoon prayer. He said: ‘And this verse was revealed: O you who have believed, indeed if you are a believer, then indeed God wills.’” A wicked person has come to you with report, so verify it, lest you harm people out of ignorance and become regretful for what you have done. Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, O you who have believed, if there comes to you a disobedient one with information… the verse, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent Al-Walid bin Uqbah bin Abi Mu’ayt, then one of the sons of Amr bin Umayyah, then one of the sons of Abi Mu’ayt, to Banu al-Mustaliq, to collect alms from them. When the report reached them, they rejoiced and went out to meet the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. When Al-Walid was told that they had gone out to meet him, he returned to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said, ‘O Messenger of God, Banu al-Mustaliq have refused to pay alms.’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, became extremely angry. While he was thinking about attacking them, a delegation came to him and said, ‘O Messenger of God, we were told that your messenger has returned halfway, and we feared that he had rejected a letter that came to him from you because of his anger with us. We seek refuge in God from his anger and the anger of…’” His Messenger, so God revealed their excuse in the Book, saying, O you who have believed, if there comes to you a disobedient one with information, investigate, lest you harm a people out of ignorance and become, over what you have done, regretful. Muhammad ibn Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, “Concerning His statement, ‘If a wicked person comes to you with report,’ he said: Al-Walid ibn Uqba ibn Abi Mu’ayt, whom God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent to Banu Al-Mustaliq to give them truth, so they met him with gifts, so he returned to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: Banu Al-Mustaliq have gathered to fight you.” Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, O you who have believed, if there comes to you a disobedient one with information, until he reached in ignorance, and he is the son of Abi Mu’ayt al-Walid ibn Uqbah. The Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent him as a tax collector to Banu al-Mustaliq. When they saw him, they came towards him, and he was afraid of them. He returned to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and informed him that they had apostatized from Islam. The Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent Khalid ibn al-Walid and ordered him to verify and not to be hasty. He set out until he came to them at night, and sent his spies. When they came, they informed Khalid that they were adhering to Islam, and they heard their call to prayer and their prayer. When morning came, Khalid came to them and saw something that pleased him, so he returned to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and told him the report. Then God Almighty revealed what you hear. The Prophet of God used to say, Disclosure is from God, and haste is from Satan. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada: O you who have believed, if there comes to you a disobedient one with information, and he mentioned something similar. Muhammad bin Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Hilal al-Wazzan, on the authority of Ibn Abi Layy, regarding his statement, O you who have believed, if there comes to you a disbeliever with information, verify it, he said: It was revealed about al-Walid bin Uqba bin Abi Mu’ayt. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Hamid, on the authority of Hilal Al-Ansari, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Abi Laila: If a wicked person comes to you with report, he said: It was revealed about Al-Walid bin Uqba when he sent to Banu Al-Mustaliq. He said: Salamah narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, on the authority of Yazid ibn Ruman, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent Al-Walid ibn [Uqbah ibn] Abi Mu’ayt to Banu al-Mustaliq after they had embraced Islam. When they heard of him, they rode to him. When he heard of them, he was afraid of them, so he returned to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and informed him that the people had intended to kill him and had withheld the charity they had received from him. The Muslims kept mentioning their invasion until the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, intended to invade them. While they were doing that, their delegation came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, we heard of your messenger when you sent him to us, so we went out to meet him to honor him and to pay him the charity we had received from him. He kept on returning, and we were informed that he was claiming to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that we had gone out to meet him to fight him, but by God, we had not gone out for that purpose. So God revealed concerning Al-Walid ibn Uqbah and them: O you who have believed, if there comes to you a disobedient one with information… He said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent a man from among his companions to a people to give them charity. The man came to them, and there was enmity between him and them in the pre-Islamic era. When he came to them, they welcomed him, acknowledged the zakat, and gave them what they were owed. The man returned to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, the Banu so-and-so refused to give charity and turned away from Islam. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, became angry and sent to them. They came to him and said: Have you refused to give zakat and expelled my messenger? They said: By God, we did not do that, and we know that you are the Messenger of God, and we would not have changed or refused God’s right in our wealth. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not give them charity. So God revealed this verse and excused them.” And His statement, lest you harm a people out of ignorance, means, Then be careful lest you harm a people innocent of what they have accused of, through a crime committed out of your ignorance, and become regretful over what you have done, meaning, regretting what you have done. You inflicted upon them the crime with which you inflicted upon them.
49:7: God Almighty says to the companions of the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: Know, O believers in God and His Messenger, that among you is the Messenger of God. So fear God lest you say falsehood and fabricate lies, for God informs him of your report and makes him aware of your information, and his people are on the right path in their affairs. And His statement, If he had obeyed you in much of the matter, you would have been cursed, God Almighty says: If the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had acted in accordance with your opinions and accepted from you what you said to him, he would have obeyed you. You means: he would have suffered hardship and difficulty in many matters because of his obedience to you. If he had obeyed you, because he used to make mistakes in his actions, as if he had accepted what Al-Walid ibn Uqbah said about Banu Al-Mustaliq: They had apostatized, refused to pay the zakat, and gathered forces to attack the Muslims. So he attacked them and killed some of them, and seized their blood and wealth. He had killed, and you had killed, those whom it was not permissible for him or for you to kill, and he had taken and seized from the wealth of a Muslim people what it was not permissible for him or for you to take, so he had suffered from God because of that. But God has endeared faith to you in God and His Messenger. So you obey the Messenger of God and follow him, and God thereby protects you from the hardship that if you had not obeyed him and followed him, and he had obeyed you, he would have suffered and befallen you. And His statement, And He has made it pleasing in your hearts, meaning: And made faith good, so you believed. And He has made hateful to you disbelief in God, and immorality, meaning lying, disobedience, meaning doing what God has forbidden in opposition to the command of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and neglecting what God has commanded. Those are the ones who are rightly guided, meaning: These are the ones to whom God has made faith beloved, and has made it pleasing in their hearts, and has made hateful to disbelief, immorality, and disobedience. Those are the ones who are rightly guided and follow the path of truth. And His statement, Blessing and favor from God, means: But God has endeared faith to you, and bestowed upon you this blessing which He considered a favor from Him, and a kindness and favor from Him that He bestowed upon you. And God is Knowing and Wise, means: God has knowledge of who among you does good and who does evil, who is worthy of God’s favor and favor, and who is not worthy of it, and there is wisdom in His management of His creation, and His dispensing of them as He wills of His judgment. And similar to what we said in the interpretation of His statement, “And know that among you is the Messenger of God. If he were to obey you in much of the matter, you would be in trouble,” the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada: And know that among you is the Messenger of God… the verse until he reached you have been cursed. These are the companions of the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. If the Prophet of God had obeyed them in many matters, you would have been cursed. By God, you are the most foolish in opinion and the most reckless in mind. The most suspicious man is his opinion, and he who takes the advice of the Book of God is trustworthy for whoever takes it and adheres to it. Anything other than the Book of God is deception. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us: Muammar recited Qatadah’s verse, If he obeyed you in much of the matter, you would be cursed. He said: You are the most foolish in opinion and the most foolish in dreams. A man may be accused of his opinion, but he seeks advice from the Book of God. And also as we said in the interpretation of his saying, But God has endeared faith to you, they said. Who said that? Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said about His statement, He has made faith beloved to you and has beautified it in your hearts, he said: He has made it beloved to you and made it beautiful in their hearts. And similar to what we said in the interpretation of His statement, “And He has made hateful to you disbelief, immorality, and disobedience. Those are the [rightly] guided. * A bounty and favor from God.” They also said. Who said that? Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, And He has made disbelief and immorality hateful to you, he said: Lying and disobedience. He said: Disobedience to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Those are the ones who are rightly guided. Where did this come from? He said: A favor and blessing from God. He said: And the hypocrites, God called them all liars in the Qur’an. He said: And immorality means lying in the entire Book of God.
49:8: God Almighty says: “A bounty and a blessing from God. God is Knowing and Wise.”
49:9: God Almighty says: If two groups of the people of faith fight, then make peace between them, O believers, by calling to the rule of God’s Book, and being satisfied with what is in it for and against them. That is making peace between them with justice. But if one of them transgresses against the other means: If these two groups refuse to respond to God’s rule for and against them, and transgresses what God has made just between His creation, and the other responds, then fight the one that transgresses means: Fight the one that transgresses and refuses to respond to God’s rule. until it returns to the command of God means: until it returns to the rule of God that He has made in His Book between His creation. “But if it returns, then make peace between them with justice” means: If the transgressor returns after you have fought them to being satisfied with God’s rule in His Book, then make peace between it and the other group that fought it with justice meaning with fairness between them. That is the rule of God in His Book that He has made just between His creation. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ali told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, “And if two parties among the believers should fight, then make peace between them. But if one of them oppresses the other, then fight against the one that oppresses until it returns to the command of God.” Indeed, God, the Exalted, commanded the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the believers, if two parties among the believers should fight, to call them to the rule of God and to be fair to one another. If they respond, then judge between them according to the Book of God, until the oppressed is judged against the oppressor. Whoever among them refuses to respond is a transgressor. So it is the duty of the leader of the believers to strive against them and fight them until they return to the command of God and acknowledge the rule of God. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahib told us: Ibn Zayd said about His statement, And if two parties among the believers should fight… to the end of the verse: This is a command from God that He commanded the rulers to do, as if there were a group of people among them, and He commanded them to make peace between them. If they refuse, then fight the rebellious group until they return to the command of God. When they return, make peace between them, and tell them that the believers are brothers, so make peace between your two brothers. He said: No one fights the rebellious group except the leader. He mentioned that this verse was revealed about two groups from the Aws and Khazraj tribes who fought over some of the issues they had disputed, which I will mention, God willing. The narration mentioned that: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told me: Mu’tamir ibn Sulayman told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Anas, who said: It was said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Why don’t you go to Abdullah ibn Ubayy? He said: “He went to him and rode a donkey, and the Muslims set off. It is a salty land. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to him, he said: “Go away from me, for by God, the stench of your donkey has bothered me.” A man from the Ansar said: By God, the stench of the Messenger of God’s donkey is better smelling than you. A man from his people became angry on behalf of Abdullah ibn Ubayy. He said: And each of their companions became angry. He said: “There was fighting between them with palm branches, hands, and sandals. We were informed that the verse was revealed concerning them: ‘And if two parties among the believers should quarrel, then make peace between them.’” Abu Hasin Abdullah bin Ahmad bin Yunus told me: Ubaydhar told us: Hasin told me on the authority of Abu Malik regarding his statement, And if two parties among the believers should fight, then make settlement between them, he said: Two men fought, and one of them became angry with his people, and the other with his people, so they gathered and started beating each other with sandals until it was almost a fight between them - then God revealed this verse. Abu Kurayb told us: Hisham told us, on the authority of Hisin, on the authority of Abu Malik, regarding his statement, And if two parties among the believers should fight, he said: There was a fight between them without weapons. Yaqub told me: Hisham told us: Hisin told us on the authority of Abu Malik regarding his statement, “And if two parties among the believers should fight, then make peace between them,” he said: They were two tribes of the Ansar, and there was a dispute between them without weapons. Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, “And if two parties among the believers should fight, then make peace between them,” he said: Their fighting was with sandals and sticks, so he ordered them to make peace between them. He said: Mahrān narrated to us, he said: Al-Mubarak ibn Fadala narrated to us on the authority of Al-Hasan: And if two parties among the believers should fight, he said: There would be a dispute between two groups, so he would call them to judgment, but they would refuse to respond, so God revealed: “And if two parties among the believers should fight, then make peace between them. But if one of them oppresses the other, then fight against the one that oppresses until it returns to the command of God,” meaning: Bring them to judgment, so their fight was to repel. He said: Mihran told us, he said: Sufyan told us on the authority of al-Suddi, “And if two parties among the believers should fight, then make peace between them.” He said: There was a woman from the Ansar called Umm Zayd who was married to a man, and there was something between her and her husband, so he took her up to an upper room and said to them: Be careful. Her people heard about that, so they came and his people came, and they fought with their hands and sandals. report of that reached the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he came to make peace between them, and the Qur’an was revealed: “And if two parties among the believers should fight, then make peace between them. But if one of them oppresses the other,” he said: Exercise means not accepting the peace agreement of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, or the judgment of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And if two parties among the believers should fight, he said: The Aws and the Khazraj fought each other with sticks. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And if two parties among the believers should fight… the verse. It was mentioned to us that it was revealed about two men from the Ansar who were disputing over a right between them. One of them said to the other: I will seize him by force, because of his large clan. The other called him to bring him to the Prophet of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) for judgment, but he refused to follow him. This continued until they pushed each other, and some of them even attacked each other with their hands and sandals. There was no fighting with swords. So God commanded that you fight until you return to the command of God, the Book of God, and to the judgment of His Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). It is not as the people of doubts and innovations, and the scholars of Al-Farra’ interpreted it, that it is permissible for you to kill a believer. By God, God has magnified the sanctity of the believer to the point that He has forbidden you to think anything but good of your brother, saying: The believers are but brothers. (al-Hujurat 49:10)… the verse. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Hasan, that there was a dispute among some Muslims, until they started to fight with their sandals and hands. So God revealed about them: And if two parties among the believers should fight, Qatada said: There were two men between whom there was a right, so they argued with each other. One of them said: I will take him by force, because of his large clan. The other said: Between me and you is the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. So they argued until there was a clash between them with sandals and hands. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said: Abdullah ibn Abbas told me: Zayd was killed because of the statement of God, the Most High: “And if two parties among the believers should fight, then make peace between them.” These two men were fighting from among the people of Islam, or one group after another, or one tribe after another, so God commanded the leaders of the Muslims to judge between them with the truth that He revealed in His Book: either retaliation and kindling, or blood money and a donkey, or pardon. But if one of them oppresses the other, after that the Muslims were with the oppressed against the oppressor, until he returned to the command of God and was pleased with it. Ibn al-Barqi told us: Ibn Abi Maryam told us: Nafi` ibn Yazid told us: Ibn Jurayj told us: Ibn Shihab and others, adding hadiths to one another, said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sat in a gathering in which there was `Abdullah ibn Rawahah and `Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, left, `Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul said: ‘His donkey’s dung has bothered us and has blocked our spirits.’ There was something between him and Ibn Rawahah until they came out with weapons. Then he came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he came to them and separated them.” That is why `Abdullah ibn Ubayy says: Whenever your master is your opponent, you will be wronged and those with whom you wrestle will defeat you. He said: So this verse was revealed about them: And if two parties among the believers should fight. And His statement, And be just, God Almighty says: And be just, O believers, in your judgments between those between whom you judge, by not exceeding in your judgments the judgment of God and the judgment of His Messenger. Indeed, God loves those who are just, meaning: God loves those who are just in their judgments, who judge between His creation with justice.
49:10: God the Almighty says to the people of faith in Him: The believers are but brothers in religion. “So make peace between your two brothers” if they fight, by compelling them to adhere to the rule of God and the rule of His Messenger. The meaning of two brothers in this context is: every two people of faith who fight. The reciters of the regions read it with the dual vowel. It was reported from Ibn Sirin that he read between your brothers with the letter nun according to the plural form, and this is correct from the Arabic perspective, but it is contrary to what the reciters of the regions do, so I do not like to read it with it. And fear God that you may receive mercy. God the Almighty says: And fear God, O people, by fulfilling His obligations upon you in reconciling between the two people of faith who fight with justice, and in other obligations, and avoiding His transgressions, so that your Lord may have mercy upon you and pardon you for your past crimes if you obey Him, follow His commands and prohibitions, and fear Him by obeying Him.
49:11: He says: The Most High said: O you who have believed in God and His Messenger, let not a believing people ridicule [another] believing people. Perhaps they may be better than them. He says: The one being ridiculed among them is better than the ridiculers. Nor let women ridicule [other] women. He says: Nor let believing women ridicule believing women. Perhaps the one being ridiculed among them may be better than the ridiculers. The commentators differed regarding the mockery that God forbade believers from in this verse. Some of them said: It is the mockery of the rich by the poor. He forbade mocking the poor for their poverty. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Ibn Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh on the authority of Mujahid: A people should not mock another people. He said: A people should not mock another people, such that a poor man asks a rich man, or a poor man, and if a man does him a favor for something, then there is nothing wrong with him, so he should not mock him. Others said: Rather, this is a prohibition from God for those who concealed their faults from among the people of faith to mock those among them who uncovered their faults in this world. Who said that? Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said about His statement, O you who have believed, let not a people ridicule [another] people; perhaps they may be better than them; nor let women ridicule [other] women; perhaps they may be better than them, he said: Perhaps a man stumbles when he commits a sin; perhaps he is better than them. If his stumble becomes apparent, and you cover up your stumble, perhaps what became apparent will be better for him in the Hereafter with God, and what you cover up will be worse for you. How do you know? Perhaps He will not forgive you. He said: So the man was forbidden from that, and he said: Let not a people ridicule another people; perhaps they may be better than them. And he said the same about women. The correct thing to say about this, in my opinion, is that God’s prohibition of believers from mocking one another encompasses all meanings of mockery. It is not permissible for a believer to mock another believer, whether for his poverty, or for a sin he has committed, or for any other reason. And His statement, And do not find fault with one another, means, the Most High says: And do not backbite one another, O believers, and do not slander one another. And He said, Do not find fault with one another, making the one who finds fault with his brother find fault with himself, because the believers are like one man in what they are obligated to do for one another of improving one another's affairs, seeking their betterment, and loving good for one another. For this reason, it was narrated from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: The believers are like a single body; if one part of it is ill, the rest of the body feels pain and sleeplessness. This is similar to His statement, "O you who have believed, do not consume one another's wealth unjustly, except [in lawful] business by mutual consent. And do not kill yourselves," meaning: and do not kill one another. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And do not insult one another, he said: Do not backbite. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And do not criticize one another, meaning: Do not insult one another. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, similarly. Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me: On the authority of his father: On the authority of Ibn Abbas: His statement, And do not criticize one another, means: Do not criticize one another. His statement, And do not insult one another by nicknames, means: Do not call one another by nicknames. Insulting and nicknames have the same meaning. The plural of nabz is anbaz, and the plural of nickname is alabaqban. The commentators differed regarding the nicknames that God forbade calling one another by in this verse. Some of them said: What is meant by it are the nicknames that are disliked to be used by the one being called. They said: This verse was revealed about a people who had names in the pre-Islamic era, and when they became Muslims, they were forbidden to call one another by the names that were disliked by those names that they were called by in the pre-Islamic era. Who said that? Humayd ibn Mas`adah narrated: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal narrated: Dawud narrated on the authority of `Amir: Abu Jubayrah ibn al-Dahhak said: “This verse was revealed about us, Banu Salamah. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) came and there was not a man among us who did not have two or three names. So if a man called another man by his name, we would say: O Messenger of God, he gets angry at this. So this verse was revealed: ‘And do not insult one another by nicknames’...the entire verse.” Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told me: Abd al-Wahhab told us: Dawud told us, on the authority of Aamer, on the authority of Abu Jubayrah ibn al-Dahhak, who said: “The people of the Age of Ignorance used to call men by names. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, called a man by one of those names, and they said: O Messenger of God, he gets angry about this. So God revealed: ‘And do not insult one another by nicknames. Evil is the name of disobedience after faith.’” Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Ibn Abd Al-A’la told us: Dawud told us on the authority of Amer: Abu Jubayrah Ibn Al-Dahhak told us, and he mentioned something similar on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Yaqub told me: Ibn Ulayyah told us: Dawud told us on the authority of Al-Sha’bi: Abu Jubayrah ibn Ad-Dahhak told me: “The verse, ‘And do not insult one another by nicknames,’ was revealed concerning Banu Salamah. He said: ‘The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came and there was not a man among us who did not have two or three names. He would call a man, and his mother would say, ‘He gets angry with this one.’ So ‘And do not insult one another by nicknames,’ was revealed. And he said on another occasion: If he called one by this name, it would be said, ‘O Messenger of God, he gets angry with this one.’ So the verse was revealed.” Others said: Rather, it is a Muslim man saying to a Muslim man: You are a sinner, you are a fornicator. Who said that? Muhammad bin Al-Sarri told us: Abu Al-Ahwas told us on the authority of Hisin who said: I asked Ikrimah about the statement of God, And do not insult one another by nicknames. He said: It is when a man says to another man, O hypocrite! or O infidel! Yaqub bin Ibrahim told us: Hisham told us: Hisin told us on the authority of Ikrimah regarding his statement, And do not insult one another by nicknames, he said: It is when a man says to another man, O wicked one, O hypocrite. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Hisin, on the authority of Ikrimah: And do not insult one another by nicknames. He said: O wicked one, O infidel. He said: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Mujahid or Ikrimah, And do not insult one another by nicknames. He said: A man says to another man: O wicked one, O infidel. Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And do not insult one another by nicknames, he said: A man was called an infidel while he was a Muslim. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And do not insult one another by nicknames, he says to the man: Do not kill for your Muslim brother: That one is a sinner, that one is a hypocrite. God forbade the Muslim from that and presented it in it. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada: And do not insult one another by nicknames. He said: Do not say to your Muslim brother: O sinner, O hypocrite. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said about His statement, And do not insult one another by nicknames, he said: Calling him for bad deeds after Islam is an adulterer and a sinner. Others said: Rather, it is calling a man an infidel after Islam, and a sinner and doing ugly deeds after repentance. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me: On the authority of his father: On the authority of Ibn Abbas: “And do not insult one another by nicknames. Evil is the name of disobedience after faith”… the verse. He said: Insulting one another by nicknames is when a man commits bad deeds and then repents from them and returns to the truth, so God forbade insulting oneself for what he did in the past. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar: Al-Hasan said: A Jew or a Christian would convert to Islam, and he would be called by nicknames, and it would be said to him: O Jew, O Christian, and they were forbidden from doing that. What I think is the most correct interpretation of this is that God, the Exalted, forbade the believers from calling one another by nicknames. Calling one another by nicknames is when a person calls his companion by a name or description he dislikes. God made this prohibition general and did not specify some nicknames over others. Therefore, it is not permissible for any Muslim to call his brother by a name or description he dislikes. If this is the case, then all the interpretations we have mentioned are correct. Some of them are not more correct than others, because this is one of the things that God forbade the Muslims from calling one another by nicknames. And His statement, What a bad name is immorality after having believed, God Almighty says: And whoever does what We have forbidden, and proceeds to disobey Us after his belief, and mocks the believers, and slanders his believing brother, and calls him by nicknames, then he is immoral. What a bad name is immorality, meaning: Do not do it, lest you deserve to be called immoral if you do it. What a bad name is immorality. He left out mentioning what we described of the speech, contenting himself with indicating it with What a bad name is immorality. Ibn Zayd used to say something about that. Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb told us, saying: Ibn Zayd recited: How evil is the name of immorality after faith. He said: How evil is the name of immorality when you call someone immoral after Islam, while he is a Muslim. He said: The people of this opinion are the Mu'tazila. They said: We do not declare him an unbeliever as the people of desires declared him an unbeliever, nor do we call him a believer, as the group said, but we call him by his name: if he is a thief, then he is a thief. If he is a traitor, then they call him a traitor. If he is an adulterer, then they call him an adulterer. He said: So they separated from the two groups, the people of desires and the group. Neither the ones said what these said nor the ones said what these said. So they were called Mu'tazila. Ibn Zayd directed the interpretation of his statement, How evil is the name of immorality after faith, to the one who is called an immoral person while he has repented from his immorality, so that is an evil name for him. Other interpretations are more appropriate to speak about, because God preceded with the prohibition of what He preceded with the prohibition of in the beginning of this verse, so what is more appropriate is to end it with a threat to the one who proceeds with his transgression, or with the ugly nature of his doing what he did that was prohibited, not to inform about the ugliness of what the repentant person did before his repentance, since the verse did not begin with the information about his doing what he did before repenting of the ugly thing, so it ends at the end with a threat to him or with the ugly thing. And His statement, And whoever does not repent - then it is those who are the wrongdoers, God Almighty says: And whoever does not repent from calling his brother by the nicknames that God has forbidden him to be called by, or slandering him, or mocking him, then it is those who have wronged themselves, and have brought upon themselves the punishment of God by doing what He has forbidden them to do. Ibn Zayd used to say about this: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said about His statement, And whoever does not repent - then it is those who are the wrongdoers, he said: And whoever does not repent from that immorality - then it is those who are the wrongdoers.
49:12: God the Most High says: O you who have believed in God and His Messenger, do not assume too much suspicion of the believers, that is, think ill of them, for the one who assumes it is not right. And God the Most High said: Avoid much suspicion, and He did not say: all suspicion, as He had given permission to the believers to assume good of one another, saying: Why, when you heard it, did not the believing men and believing women think good of one another and say, ‘This is an obvious falsehood?’ (al-Nur 24:12) So God the Most High gave permission to the believers to assume good of one another and to say it, even if they were not certain of what was said about them. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about the meaning of that. Who said that? Ali told me: Abu Saleh told me: Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, O you who have believed, avoid much [negative] assumption, meaning: God forbade the believer from thinking ill of another believer. His saying, Some suspicion is a sin, means that if a believer suspects evil of another believer, not good, then it is a sin, because God has forbidden him from doing so, so doing what God has forbidden is a sin. And His statement, And do not spy, means: Do not seek out the faults of others, nor search for their secrets, seeking thereby to expose their faults. Rather, be content with what is apparent to you of his affair, and praise or blame him based on that, not with what you do not know of his secrets. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ali told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And do not spy, meaning: God forbade the believer from following the faults of another believer. Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And do not spy, he said: Take what is apparent to you and leave what God has concealed. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding His statement, “O you who have believed, avoid much [negative] assumption. Indeed, some assumption is sin. And do not spy.” Do you know what spying or espionage is? It is to follow or seek out your brother’s fault in order to learn his secret. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us on the authority of Sufyan: And do not spy. He said: Search. Yunus urged me, saying: Ibn Wahb told us, saying: Ibn Zayd said about the statement of God, “O you who have believed, avoid much [negative] assumption. Indeed, some assumption is sin. And do not spy,” he said: So that I may look into it and ask about it, so that I may know whether it is true or false. He said: So God called it spying. He said: He spies as dogs spy. And he recited the statement of God, And do not spy or backbite each other. His statement, And do not backbite one another, means: Do not say things about one another behind the backs of dogs. The one about whom that is said would hate to have it said to his face. In a similar manner to what we said about that, the hadith came from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, and the people of interpretation said. Mention of who said that, and the trace of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: Yazid bin Mukhallad Al-Rasiti told me: Khalid bin Abdullah Al-Tahhan told us, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Ala’ bin Abd Al-Rahman, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about backbiting, and he said: It is that you say about your brother what is wrong with him. If you are truthful, then you have backbitten him, and if you are lying, then you have slandered him.” Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Buzay` told us: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal told us: Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq told us, on the authority of al-`Ala` ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad bin Ja`far told us: Shu`bah told us: I heard Al-`Ala’ narrating, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Do you know what backbiting is? They said: God and His Messenger know best. He said: It is mentioning about your brother in a way that is not true. He said: What if what I say about my brother is true? He said: If what you say is true, then you have backbitten him, and if what you say is true, then you have slandered him. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Saeed bin Al-Rabi’ told us: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Al-Abbas, on the authority of a man who heard Ibn Umar say: If you mention something about a man, then you have backbitten him, and if you mention something about him that is not in him, then you have slandered him. Shu’bah said another time: If you mention something about him that is not in him, then it is a slander. Abu Musa said: He is Abbas Al-Jariry. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Sulayman, on the authority of Abdullah bin Marra, on the authority of Masruq, who said: If you mention the worst things about a man, then you have backbitten him, and if you mention things about him that are not in him, then you have slandered him. Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu al-Dhaha, on the authority of Masruq, who said: If you say the worst thing about a man, then you have backbitten him, and if you say something that is not true, then you have slandered him. Abu Kuraib told us: Omar bin Ubaid told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Al-Dhaha, on the authority of Masruq, who said: Backbiting is when someone says the worst thing he knows about him, and slander is when someone says something that is not true. Yunus bin Abdul A’la told us: Ibn Wahb told us: Mu’awiyah bin Salih told me, on the authority of Katheer bin Al-Harith, on the authority of Al-Qasim, the freed slave of Mu’awiyah, who said: I heard Ibn Umm Abd say: No one has taken a morsel worse than backbiting a believer. If he says something about him that he knows, then he has backbitten him, and if he says something about him that he does not know, then he has slandered him. Abu Al-Sa’ib told us: Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Muslim, on the authority of Masruq, who said: If you mention something about a man, then you have backbitten him, but if you mention something about him that is not true, then that is slander. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Al-Mu’tamir told us: I heard Yunus on the authority of al-Hasan that he said about backbiting: It is to mention about your brother what you know of his bad deeds, but if you mention about him what is not in him, then that is slander. Ibn Abi Al-Shawarib told us: Abd Al-Wahid bin Ziyad told us: Sulayman Al-Shaibani told us: Hassan bin Al-Mukhariq told us that a woman entered upon Aisha, and when she stood up to leave, Aisha pointed with her hand to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, meaning that she was short, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: You have backbitten her. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Abu Dawud told us: Abu Dawud told us: Shu’bah told us on the authority of Abu Ishaq, who said: If someone with a amputated hand passed by you and you said: That is the amputated one, then that would be backbiting on your part. He said: I heard Mu’awiyah ibn Qurra say that. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad bin Ja`far told us: Shu`bah told us: I heard Mu`awiyah bin Qurrah say: If a man whose hand had been amputated passed by you and you were to say to him: He has been amputated, you would have slandered him. He said: I mentioned that to Abu Ishaq Al-Hamadani and he said: He is telling the truth. Jabir bin Al-Kurdi told me: Ibn Abi Uwais told us: My brother Abu Bakr told me, on the authority of Hammad bin Abi Hamid, on the authority of Musa bin Wardan, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, “A man stood in front of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they saw weakness in his standing, so they said: O Messenger of God, what made so-and-so weak? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: You have eaten your brother and backbitten him.” Abu Kuraib narrated: Uthman ibn Saeed narrated: Habban ibn Ali al-Anzi narrated: Muthanna ibn Sabah narrated: Amr ibn Shuaib narrated: Muadh ibn al-Jabal said: “We were with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) when the people mentioned a man and said: ‘He only eats what he is fed, and he only rides what he is given to ride, and how weak he is.’ The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: ‘You have backbitten your brother.’ They said: ‘O Messenger of God, is backbiting him such that we should speak about him?’ He said: ‘It is enough for you to speak about your brother as he is.’” Abu Kuraib told us: Khalid bin Muhammad bin Jaafar told us, on the authority of Al-Ala’, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If you mention your brother in a way that he dislikes, then if what you say is true in him, then you have backbitten him, and if what you say is not true in him, then you have slandered him. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada who said: We were told that backbiting is to mention your brother in a way that disgraces him, and to criticize him for what he has, and if you lie about him then that is slander. And His statement, Would any of you like to eat the flesh of his dead brother? You would hate it. God Almighty says to the believers: Would any of you, O people, like to eat the flesh of his dead brother? If you do not like that and hate it, because God has forbidden that to you, then likewise you should not like to backbite him during his life. So hate backbiting him when he is alive, just as you hated his flesh when he is dead, because God has forbidden backbiting him when he is alive, just as He has forbidden eating his flesh when he is dead. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ali told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, “And do not backbite one another. Would any of you like to eat the flesh of his dead brother?” He said: God has forbidden the believer to backbite a believer about anything, just as He has forbidden dead meat. Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: Would any of you like to eat the flesh of his dead brother? They said: We dislike that. He said: That is how it is, so fear God. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada: Would any of you like to eat the flesh of his dead brother? You would hate it. He said: Just as you would hate to eat from a wormy corpse if you found it, so too would you hate to backbite him while he is alive. And His statement, “And fear God. Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful.” God Almighty says: So fear God, O people, and fear His punishment by refraining from what He has forbidden you from, such as thinking ill of your believing brother, following up on his faults, spying on what he has concealed from him, backbiting him in a way you would dislike, intending to defame and disgrace him, and other such matters that your Lord has forbidden you from. Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful. He says: God will return to His servant what He loves if the servant returns to his Lord to what He loves from him, and He is Merciful to him by punishing him for a sin he committed after he has repented from it. The reciters differed in their recitation of the statement, his brother’s flesh is dead. The majority of the reciters of Medina read it with the heavy dead, and the majority of the reciters of Kufa and Basra read it dead with the light dead. They are two readings that are known to us and have similar meanings, so whichever one the reciter recites, he is correct.
49:13: God Almighty says: O mankind, indeed We created you from a male fluid from men and a female fluid from women. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Abu Hisham told us: Ubayd God ibn Musa told us: Uthman ibn al-Aswad told us on the authority of Mujahid, who said: God created the child from the man’s semen and the woman’s semen, and He, the Blessed and Exalted, said: O mankind, indeed We have created you from a male and a female. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us: Uthman bin Al-Aswad told us on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Indeed, We created you from a male and a female, he said: God did not create the child except from the sperm of the man and the woman together, because God says, We created you from a male and a female. And His statement, And We have made you peoples and tribes that you may know one another, means: And We have made you related, so some of you are related to others by distant lineage, and some of you are related to others by close lineage. So the one who is related by distant lineage is the one who is not related by the peoples of the peoples, and that is if it is said to a man from the Arabs: From which people are you? He says: I am from Mudar, or from Rabi’ah. As for the people of close lineage, they are the people of the tribes, and they are like Tamim from Mudar, and Bakr from Rabi’ah, and the closest tribes are the clans, and they are like Shaiban from Bakr and Darim from Tamim, and something similar to that is the saying of Ibn Ahmar al-Bahili: From the people of Hamdan, or Saad Al-Ashirah, or Khawlan, or Madhhij, they were excited for him In a similar vein to what we said about the meaning of His statement, And We made you into peoples and tribes, he said: The people of interpretation. Who said that? Abu Kurayb told us: Abu Bakr bin Ayyash told us: Abu Hasin told us on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And We made you peoples and tribes. He said: Peoples are groups, and tribes are clans. Khallad bin Aslam told us: Abu Bakr bin Ayyash told us, on the authority of Abu Hasin, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement, And We made you peoples and tribes, he said: Peoples means the group. Khallad said: Abu Bakr said: The great tribes, like Banu Tamim, and the tribes mean the clans. Abu Kurayb told us: Abu Atiyah told us: Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Hasin, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair: And We made you peoples and tribes. He said: The peoples are the masses, and the tribes are the individuals. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Peoples, he said: distant lineage. And tribes less than that. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada: And We made you peoples and tribes. He said: Peoples are distant relatives, and tribes are like his saying: So-and-so is from the Banu So-and-so, and so-and-so is from the Banu So-and-so. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: And We made you into nations. He said: It refers to distant lineage. He said: And the tribes: as you hear it said: So-and-so is from the Banu so-and-so. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, And We made you into nations, that he said: As for the nations, they are distant relatives. Some of them said: The al-Nas 114:the thighs. Who said that? Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Hasin, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair: And We made you peoples and tribes. He said: The peoples are the clans, and the tribes are the tribes. Others said: Peoples are clans, and tribes are thighs. Who said that? Yahya bin Talha told me: Abu Bakr bin Ayyash told us, on the authority of Abu Hasin, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And We made you peoples and tribes. He said: The peoples are the clans, and the tribes are the large thighs. Others said: Peoples: lineages. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And We made you peoples and tribes. He said: Peoples: tribes: like lineages. And His statement, So that you may know one another, means: So that you may know one another in lineage. God Almighty says: We have only made these peoples and tribes for you, O people, so that you may know one another in terms of closeness of kinship and distance from one another, not for any virtue you may have in that, or for the sake of drawing you closer to God. Rather, the most honorable of you in the sight of God is the most righteous of you. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And tribes that you may know one another. He said: We made this so that you may know one another. So-and-so, son of so-and-so, is from such-and-such.
