And His statement, The most honorable of you in the sight of God is the most righteous of you, God Almighty says: The most honorable of you, O people, in the sight of your Lord is the one who fears Him most by performing His obligations and avoiding His sins, not the one with the greatest house or the largest clan. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Lahi’ah told me, on the authority of Al-Harith bin Yazid, on the authority of Ali bin Rabah, on the authority of Uqbah bin Amir, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “People are like the handful of a sa’ which you cannot fill. God will not ask you about your lineage or your ancestry on the Day of Resurrection. The most honorable of you in the sight of God is the most righteous of you.” Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Lahi’ah told me, on the authority of Al-Harith bin Yazid, on the authority of Ali bin Rabah, on the authority of Uqbah bin Amir, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Your lineage is not a means of insulting anyone. You are the children of Adam, the measure of which you have not filled. No one has any superiority over anyone except through religion or doing a righteous deed. It is enough for a man to be vulgar, vulgar, miserly, and cowardly.” Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me: Ibn Ulayyah told us on the authority of Ibn Jurayj who said: I heard Ata’ say: Ibn Abbas said: There are three verses that people denied: permission in its entirety, and He said: The most honorable of you in the sight of God is the most righteous of you. And the people said: The most honorable of you is the one with the greatest house. And Ata’ said: I forgot the third. And His statement, Indeed, God is All-Knowing, means that God Almighty says: O people, God is All-Knowing of the most pious of you in the sight of God and the most honorable of you in His sight. He is All-Knowing of you and your interests, and other than that of your affairs. Nothing is hidden from Him.
49:14: God Almighty says: The Bedouins said: We believe in God and His Messenger, so we are believers. God said to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, to them: You have not believed and you are not believers, but say: We have submitted. He mentioned that this verse was revealed about the Banu Asad Bedouins. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, The Bedouins said, ‘We believe,’ he said: The Bedouins of Banu Asad bin Khuzaymah. The commentators differed about the reason why it was said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: “Tell these Bedouins: Say, ‘We have submitted,’ and do not say, ‘We believe.’” Some of them said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, only ordered this because the people had believed with their tongues, but their words had not been confirmed by their actions. So it was said to them: Say, ‘We have submitted,’ because Islam is a statement, and faith is a statement and an action. Who said that? Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of al-Zuhri: The Bedouins said, ‘We have believed.’ Say, ‘You have not believed, but say, ‘We have submitted.’ He said: Islam is the word, and faith is the action. Ibn Abd al-A'la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar, and al-Zuhri told me, on the authority of Amir ibn Sa'd, on the authority of his father, who said: "The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave to some men, but did not give anything to any other man. Sa'd said: 'O Messenger of God, you gave to so-and-so and so-and-so, but did not give anything to so-and-so, and he is a believer.' The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: 'Or a Muslim.' Until Sa'd repeated it three times, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: 'Or a Muslim.' Then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: 'I give to some men and leave out those who are dearer to me than them. I do not give them anything for fear that they will fall on their faces into the Fire.'" Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said about His statement, The desert Arabs say, ‘We believe.’ Say, ‘You have not believed.’ He said: They did not confirm their belief with their deeds. So God responded to them with, Say, ‘You have not believed; but say, ‘We have submitted.’ And He informed them that the believers are those who believed in God and His Messenger and then did not doubt, and strove with their wealth and their lives in the cause of God, those are the truthful ones. They confirmed their belief with their deeds. So whoever among them says, ‘I am a believer,’ has spoken the truth. He said: As for whoever claims to believe through words but does not act, then he has lied and is not truthful. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim: But say, ‘We have submitted.’ He said: It is Islam. Others said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered that this be said to them because they wanted to be called by the names of the emigrants before they emigrated, so God informed them that they would have the names of the Bedouins, not the names of the emigrants. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, The Bedouins said, ‘We believe.’... the verse. This is because they wanted to be called by the name of the migration, and not by the names that God had given them, and that was at the beginning of the migration, but rather for the inheritance to be given to them. Others said: They were told that because they had shown favor to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, by their conversion to Islam. So God said to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Tell them that you did not believe, but rather submitted out of fear of being taken captive and killed. Who said that? Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding His statement, The Bedouins say, ‘We believe.’ Say, ‘You have not believed.’ By my life, this verse does not include all Bedouins. There are some Bedouins who believe in God and the Last Day. Rather, it was revealed about a tribe of Bedouins who boasted about their Islam to the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. They said, We have submitted, but we did not fight you, as the Banu so-and-so and the Banu so-and-so fought you. So God said, Do not say, ‘We believe,’ but say, ‘We have submitted,’ until it reaches your hearts. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: You have not believed, but say, ‘We have submitted.’ He said: This verse does not apply to the Bedouins. There are some Bedouins who believe in God and the Last Day and consider what they spend as means of drawing closer to God. However, it applies to groups of Bedouins. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Rabah, on the authority of Abu Auf, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair: The Bedouins say, ‘We have believed.’ Say, ‘You have not believed, but say, ‘We have submitted.’ He said: We submitted out of fear of being taken captive and killed. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Mujahid: Say ‘We have submitted.’ He said: We have surrendered. Yunus narrated: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said: He recited the statement of God, Say, ‘You have not believed, but say, “We have submitted,’ meaning we have entered into peace and abandoned fighting and fighting by saying, ‘There is no god but God.’” He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I have been commanded to fight the people until they say, ‘There is no god but God.’ Then if they say, ‘There is no god but God,’ their blood and property are protected from me, except for what is due, and their reckoning is with God.” The most correct of the sayings in interpreting the statement we mentioned from Al-Zuhri is that God proceeded to these Bedouins who entered the religion by their acknowledgement of the word, and did not confirm their word with their actions, to say in general terms, We believe, without restricting their saying to that, by saying, We believe in God and His Messenger. But He commanded them to say the statement that would not be difficult for its listeners and in which the one who said it was right, which is to say, We have submitted, meaning: We have entered the religion and the wealth, and the true testimony. And His statement, And when faith has not yet entered your hearts, God Almighty says: And when knowledge of the laws of faith and the truths of its meanings has not yet entered your hearts. And His statement, And if you obey God and His Messenger, He will not deprive you of anything of your deeds, means that God, the Exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say to these Bedouins who say, We believe, but faith has not yet entered their hearts: If you obey God and His Messenger, O people, and follow His command and the command of His Messenger, and learn what He has enjoined upon you, and refrain from what He has forbidden you, He will not deprive you of anything of your deeds, meaning, He will not wrong you in any way from the reward for your deeds, nor will He diminish you in any way from their reward. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, He will not deprive you: He will not diminish you. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, He will not deprive you of anything of your deeds, meaning: He will not wrong you in any of your deeds. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said about And if you obey God and His Messenger, he said: If you confirm your faith with your deeds, that will be accepted from you. The reading of the regions is La ya’alatum min 3amalakum without a hamza or an alif, except for Abu Amr, who read it La ya’alatum with an alif, taking into consideration his statement And We did not deprive them of anything of their work At-Tur 52:21. So whoever says alat, says ya’alat. As for the others, they made that from Lat yalit, as Ru’bah ibn al-’Ajaj said: And a dewy night I walked, and it did not turn me away from its secret. I wish The correct statement in our view on this matter is what is read in Medina and Kufa as la yaltum without an alif or a hamza, in the language of those who say la yalita do not let me sleep, for two reasons: First: The consensus of the most eloquent reciters on this. Second: It is in the Mushaf without an alif, and the hamza is not dropped in such a place because it is quiescent, and when the hamza is quiescent it remains, as you say ta’murun you command and ta’akulun you eat. It is only dropped if what precedes it is quiescent. A letter in the Qur’an that comes in one language does not carry over another that comes in a different language if both languages are known in the speech of the Arabs. We have already mentioned that al-ta and la-ta are two well-known languages of their speech. And His statement, Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful, means the Most High says: Indeed, God is Forgiving, O Arabs, to whoever obeys Him and repents to Him for his past sins, so obey Him and abide by His commands and prohibitions, and He will forgive you your sins. He is Merciful to His creation who repent to Him, and He does not punish them after their repentance from their sins, for what they repented from, so repent to Him and He will have mercy on you. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada: Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful. Forgiving of many or major sins - Yazid was unsure - Merciful to His servants.
49:15: God Almighty says to the Bedouins who said, We believe, but faith has not yet entered their hearts: The believers, O people, are only those who have believed in God and His Messenger, and then have not doubted, meaning: then have not doubted the Oneness of God, nor the Prophethood of His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and have committed themselves to obeying God and obeying His Messenger, and to doing what is required of them of God's obligations without doubting that this is required of them. And strive with their wealth and their lives in the cause of God, meaning: they strive against the polytheists by spending their wealth and sacrificing their lives in striving against them, in the way God has commanded them to strive against them, and that is His way so that the word of God will be supreme, and the word of those who disbelieve will be lowest. And his saying, Those are the truthful ones, means: Those who do that are the truthful ones in their saying, We are believers, not those who entered the nation out of fear of the sword in order to protect their blood and property. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said about His statement, Those are the truthful ones, that they confirmed their faith with their deeds.
49:16: God the Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him: Say, O Muhammad, to these Bedouins who say, We believe, but faith has not yet entered their hearts: Do you know God? O people, about your religion, meaning about your obedience to your Lord? And God knows what is in the heavens and what is on the earth. He says: And God, whom you know that you are believers, is All-Knowing of everything in the seven heavens and the seven earths. Nothing of it is hidden from Him. So how can you know Him about your religion and the faith that you are upon, while nothing is hidden from Him, in the heavens or the earth, so what you are upon of religion is hidden from Him? And God is Knowing of all things. He says: And God is All-Knowing of everything that was and is and of what will be. This is a command from God to these Bedouins to forbid them from lying and saying other than what they are upon in their religion. He says: God is all-knowing and encompasses everything, so beware of saying anything contrary to what He knows in your hearts, lest you be punished, for nothing is hidden from Him.
49:17: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: These Bedouins, O Muhammad, have bestowed upon you a favor by converting to Islam. “Say, ‘Do not bestow upon me your Islam. Rather, God bestows upon you that He has guided you to faith.’” He says: Rather, God bestows upon you, O people, that He has guided you to faith in Him and in His Messenger, if you should be truthful. He says: If you are truthful in what you say, ‘We have believed,’ then it is God who bestowed upon you a favor by guiding you to Him. So do not bestow upon me a favor by your Islam. He mentioned that these Bedouins from Banu Asad had shown the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, a favor, and said: We believed without fighting, and we did not fight you as others did. So God revealed these verses about them. Who said that? Ibn Bashar told us: Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr, regarding this verse, They do you a favor by becoming Muslims. Are they Banu Asad? He said: That has been said. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Sahl bin Yusuf told us: Shu’bah told us on the authority of Abu Bishr: I said to Sa’id bin Jubayr, “They do you a favor by converting to Islam. Are they the Banu Asad?” He said, They claim that. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Habib ibn Abi Umrah, who said: Bishr ibn Ghalib and Labid ibn Uttar, or Bishr ibn Uttar and Labid ibn Ghalib, were sitting with Al-Hajjaj. Bishr ibn Ghalib said to Labid ibn Uttar: Indeed, those who call to you from behind the chambers… was revealed about your people, Banu Tamim. I mentioned that to Sa’id ibn Jubayr, and he said: If he had known the end of the verse, he would have answered him: They do you a favor by becoming Muslims. They said: We have become Muslims and we have not fought you, Banu Asad. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada: And do not wish that we had converted to Islam without fighting. We did not fight you as the Banu so-and-so and the Banu so-and-so fought you. So God said to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say to them: “Do not wish me to have your Islam. Rather, God has bestowed upon you a favour by guiding you to faith.” Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said about His statement, “They do you a favor by becoming Muslims. Say, ‘Do not do me a favor by becoming Muslims.’” He said: These verses were revealed about the Bedouins.
49:18: God the Almighty says: O Arabs, God knows not who among you is truthful and who is lying, and who among you has entered the religion of Islam out of desire for it, and who has entered it out of fear of our Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his soldiers. So do not teach us your religion and the secrets in your hearts, for God knows what is concealed in your hearts and what you tell yourselves, and He knows what is hidden from you. So, conceal your secrets in the heavens and the earth, and nothing of that is hidden from Him. And God is Seeing of what you do. He says: God is All-Seeing of your deeds that you do, whether you do them openly or secretly, whether you do obedience or disobedience, and He is with you in all of that, if good, then good, and if evil, then evil, and He is its equal. I deny his statement, They do you a favor because they have submitted in the accusative case because they do them a favor upon it. He mentioned that in the reading of Abdullah, it is they do you a favor because they have submitted, and that is evidence for the correctness of what we have said. If it were said: It is accusative meaning: They do you a favor because they have submitted, then that would be a correct interpretation. Some of the Arabists said: It is in the genitive case, meaning because they have submitted. As for the an in His statement, Rather, God has conferred a favor upon you that He has guided you, it is in the accusative case due to the omission of the relative clause, because the meaning of the statement is: Rather, God has conferred a favor upon you that He has guided you to faith.
